newsitem.title: INDIA: India petroleum subsidy nearly doubled in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: India petroleum subsidy nearly doubled in 1996/97.

text.p: The Indian government said on Tuesday that its total subsidy on petroleum products nearly doubled to 184.40 billion rupees ($5.15 billion) in 1996/97 (April-March) from 93.60 billion in 1995/96.

"The government provided an estimated 184.40 billion rupee petroleum subsidy in 1996/97, an increase of nearly one hundred percent over the corresponding amount in the previous year," the Finance Ministry said in a report tabled in the parliament.
The subsidy on diesel rose by 61.60 billion rupees to 83.40 billion, the ministry said.

The government said the subsidy jumped after the government rolled back by half, or 15 percent, a 30 percent hike in diesel prices announced last July. The United Front government had backtracked to appease leftist coalition partners.
"As a result, the proportion of diesel subsidy in total petroleum subsidy has increased from 6.55 percent to 45.22 percent between 1994/95 and 1996/97," it added.
The subsidy on kerosene, in which more than half of India's requirements are met by imports, rose by 21.60 billion rupees to 63.50 billion rupees, the report said. ($1=35.8 rupees)
